P10.title: Stop-hook feedback suppression in conversation
P10.note: This is a happy-cli change; browser QA cannot directly verify the cli-side filter without rebuilding packages/happy-cli, reinstalling via the dev-daemon path, and restarting happy-daemon-dev. A full verification requires both (a) cli rebuild (outside this web-only QA scope) and (b) a live session with a triggered stop-hook event. For now QA should perform the browser-side check below and flag as 'deferred-qa' if no new stop-hook strings can be triggered against the rebuilt daemon.
trigger_messages: (Optional, only if daemon was rebuilt) Provoke a stop-hook by violating a spec rule or running a long-running hook-guarded command; observe whether the suppressed feedback leaks into the conversation.
steps: Step A (browser-side evidence, always possible): Navigate to dev URL, open historical sessions, search the rendered conversation for strings like 'SPEC COVERAGE ENFORCEMENT', 'spec-verify.py', 'stop hook feedback', 'stop-hook'. Capture screenshots of any historical occurrences. Absence of new occurrences in newly-recorded sessions = positive signal.

Step B (full verification, requires daemon rebuild - out of scope for web-only cycle): Rebuild packages/happy-cli (`cd packages/happy-cli && yarn build`), restart happy-daemon-dev pointing at the new bundle, trigger a stop-hook event in a session under the rebuilt daemon, confirm the conversation view does NOT show the feedback block.

Step C: Record which historical sessions still contain stop-hook leakage (these are from PRE-fix daemon and may remain until session re-records). Distinguish pre-fix leakage (expected/accepted) from post-fix leakage (a bug).
assertions: Newly-recorded sessions running under the rebuilt daemon show NO 'SPEC COVERAGE ENFORCEMENT' or similar stop-hook feedback blocks in the user conversation.
Historical sessions may still show old feedback (pre-fix) - this is acceptable.
Dev telemetry / debug logs still retain the feedback (server-side, not asserted via UI).
P10.pass_criteria: If daemon rebuilt + new session clean: PASS. If daemon not rebuilt: DEFERRED-QA with explicit note. Any new (post-rebuild) session showing stop-hook strings = FAIL.

known_limitations: P3 and P9 depend on a Codex-flavored session existing in the dev account. If none is available, record those pipelines as 'deferred-qa' with explicit reason. Do NOT fall back to production. Do NOT fabricate Codex calls via curl/API.

P10 (5.9 stop-hook filter) is a happy-cli change. Browser-only QA cannot verify post-fix cli behavior without rebuilding packages/happy-cli and restarting happy-daemon-dev. Full verification is DEFERRED to a separate cli-rebuild cycle; browser QA performs only the evidence-gathering steps described in P10.

P6 (1M context) verification is best-effort: the dev account may not have access to a 1M-context model variant in the picker. If the picker does not expose any [1m] option, record as 'deferred-qa' with explicit reason; the code-level fix can still be cross-verified by reading modelModeOptions.ts to confirm getModelContextWindow(modelKey) returns 1000000 for [1m] keys.

Some assertions (e.g. 'matches production byte-for-byte' in P7) require referencing the production /root/happy codebase without touching it; QA uses Read on /root/happy files only, never navigates Playwright to life-ai.app.

Live-session triggering requires the dev account to have at least one active session. If none exists, QA MUST create one via the UI (+ button in sidebar, type a message, send) - NEVER via curl/api/daemon HTTP.
